entries.mechanism: The UKMOD output this comparison reads gives the Universal Credit award before the benefit cap: £1,930.72 a month here. UKMOD records the cap's reduction in a separate output, which this comparison does not read. Axiom's £1,835.00 is the award after its cap (£22,020 a year divided by 12), so the £95.72 difference is the part of UKMOD's award above the cap. Axiom's cap counts only Universal Credit and leaves out the child benefit that UKMOD's counts, so this comparison does not show whether the two agree after the cap.

display.title: UKMOD's award before the cap: couple, three children, renting

entries.mechanism: UKMOD's award is £11.73 a month lower than Axiom's. Universal Credit tapers net earnings. The comparison gives Axiom net earnings of £2,993.30 a month from the annual formula (£45,000 less £6,486 income tax and £2,594.40 National Insurance, divided by 12), so Axiom's award is £2,222.79 less 55% of the £2,566.30 by which those net earnings exceed the £427 work allowance, or £811.33. UKMOD works out National Insurance week by week. In the single-employee National Insurance comparison that method differs from the annual formula by about £4 to £6 a year, which through the 55% taper moves the award by less than £0.30 a month. The files do not yet show what causes the rest of the difference.

display.title: Net-earnings difference: couple, two children, renting, earning £45,000

entries.mechanism: At exactly 16,000 of capital the two engines apply the upper-limit boundary differently. The Axiom pipeline ends entitlement when capital is greater than or equal to 16,000 (regulation 18 encoded as a >= gate), returning nil. UKMOD applies a strict > 16,000 limit, so at exactly 16,000 it still pays a tariff-reduced award: the single standard allowance 424.90 less tariff income of 4.35 per 250 of the 10,000 of capital above the 6,000 floor (40 bands x 4.35 = 174.00) gives 250.90/month, matching UKMOD's 251.30 within the tariff-band rounding. Only the exact-threshold case is affected; capital of 6,000, 6,250 and 10,000 match on both sides and 20,000 is nil on both.
